name: Building 3D shapes and scenes
gist: Papers on creating three-dimensional objects and complete scenes, including techniques to generate parts, preserve identity, and build detailed 3D environments from descriptions.
explain: Generating 3D objects and scenes is harder than generating images for a fundamental reason: images are 2D grids and relatively simple to represent, but 3D is much more complex. A 3D object has to be valid from every angle—a car viewed from the front has to have wheels if you walk around to the side. A scene has to have spatial coherence: objects can't float in mid-air unless there's a reason, and all the perspective has to be geometrically consistent. Generating something that looks good in a static 2D render is easy compared to generating something that would actually hold up as a real 3D model.

The technical challenges are immense. How do you even represent 3D? As a grid of voxels (3D pixels)? As a point cloud (a scatter of 3D points)? As a mesh (triangles forming a surface)? As a signed distance function (a mathematical description of where surfaces are)? Each representation has tradeoffs, and none captures detail as naturally as 2D images do. How do you ensure the outputs are geometrically valid—no self-intersecting surfaces, no floating-point errors that destroy the model? How do you generate from a text description ('a wooden chair') when the model has seen millions of images but far fewer 3D assets? How do you handle identity—if asked to generate a person sitting in a chair, can you make sure the person and chair are consistent across multiple generations, not randomly different people and chairs?

Research here uses several strategies. Some papers generate 3D by treating it as multiple 2D views—generate several images of an object from different angles, then use those to reconstruct 3D. Others use intermediate geometric representations: first generate a coarse skeleton or shape, then refine it. Still others condition generation on 2D images: if you show the model a photo, it can try to generate a 3D model consistent with that photo. Papers on scene generation often focus on specific domains: rooms, outdoor environments with sky and trees, and enclosed spaces where there are clear conventions about how things arrange and relate. The work is less mature than image or video generation, and many papers are still exploring what the right approach is.

papers.title: FlashWorld: High-quality 3D Scene Generation within Seconds
papers.contribution: Generates high-quality 3D scenes from single image or text in seconds, 10-100x faster than prior works while maintaining superior rendering quality and 3D consistency.

papers.title: HIVE-3D: Hierarchical Voxel Enhancement for High-Quality 3D Scene Generation
papers.contribution: HIVE-3D achieves state-of-the-art performance generating high-resolution, high-quality 3D scenes from single scene images.

papers.title: PAT3D: Physics-Augmented Text-to-3D Scene Generation
papers.contribution: Substantially outperforms prior methods in physical plausibility, semantic accuracy, visual quality; uniquely enables simulation-ready scenes for editing and robotic manipulation.

papers.title: PhysForge: Generating Physics-Grounded 3D Assets for Interactive Virtual World
papers.contribution: Produces functionally plausible, simulation-ready assets with four-tier physical annotations from PhysDB (150,000 assets); provides robust data engine for interactive 3D content.

papers.title: Sat3DGen: Comprehensive Street-Level 3D Scene Generation from Single Satellite Image
papers.contribution: Improves geometric RMSE from 6.76m to 5.20m on VIGOR-OOD benchmark and reduces FID from ~40 to 19 without extra quality modules, supporting diverse downstream applications.

papers.title: AssetFormer: Modular 3D Assets Generation with Autoregressive Transformer
papers.contribution: AssetFormer demonstrates effectiveness in streamlining modular 3D asset creation for professional development and user-generated content scenarios with a flexible, extensible framework.

papers.title: CG-MLLM: Captioning and Generating 3D content via Multi-modal Large Language Models
papers.contribution: Significantly outperforms existing MLLMs in generating high-fidelity 3D objects, bringing high-resolution 3D content creation into LLM paradigm.

papers.title: Condition Matters in Full-head 3D GANs
papers.contribution: The method eliminates directional bias, accelerates training, and enhances global coherence of generated 3D heads compared to angle-conditioned approaches.

papers.title: Interp3D: Correspondence-aware Interpolation for Generative Textured 3D Morphing
papers.contribution: Demonstrates significant advantages over previous methods in fidelity, transition smoothness, and plausibility via quantitative metrics and human studies.

papers.title: LATO: 3D Mesh Flow Matching with Structured TOpology Preserving LAtents
papers.contribution: LATO generates complex 3D meshes with well-formed topology efficiently while avoiding isosurface extraction, outperforming prior diffusion and autoregressive approaches.

papers.title: Nano3D: A Training-Free Approach for Efficient 3D Editing Without Masks
papers.contribution: Achieves superior 3D consistency and visual quality; introduces Nano3D-Edit-100k, the first large-scale 3D editing dataset with over 100,000 high-quality pairs.

papers.title: Rethinking 3D Shape Generation: Diffusion over Superquadrics
papers.contribution: Achieves competitive surface-fidelity and distributional performance while enabling efficient generation within 0.6s per shape, supporting resolution-free point-cloud decoding, part-level editing, and constraint-based design.

papers.title: UrbanGS: Efficient and Scalable Architecture for Geometrically Accurate Large-Scene Reconstruction
papers.contribution: Achieves superior rendering quality, geometric accuracy, and memory efficiency for high-fidelity large-scale urban scene reconstruction.
